newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up as PPI soothes.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen up as PPI soothes.

text.p: U.S. stocks are seen higher as October producer prices showed inflation remains benign, heightening expectations that the Fed will hold monetary policy steady later today, analysts said. The following are their comments:
PHILIP ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT:

-- "The core is the key number. I have got to believe the market rallies on that. I would expect the Fed to take no action for both the November and December meetings. Inflation is not out there with this number."

Overall PPI rose 0.4 percent, higher than the expected 0.2 percent rise. But the core rate excluding the volatile food and energy components fell 0.3 percent, compared with the anticipated 0.1 percent rise. The October core rate was the sharpest drop since the 0.4 percent decline in October 1994.
The long bond inched up 2/32 to yield 6.44 percent, still hovering near an eight-month low. December S&P 500 index futures rose 0.20 to 732.20, indicating a modestly higher open.
ALAN ACKERMAN, MARKET STRATEGIST, FAHNESTOCK AND CO:
-- "I think the PPI is comfortable enough to rally the long bond and lure stocks a bit higher. If there are no hidden or convoluted numbers in the PPI, U.S. stocks are likely to do better".
JIM PIZZO, SENIOR INVESTMENT STRATEGIST AT OPPENHEIMER:
-- "The overall numer was stronger than expected and the core was weaker -- it might turn out to be a wash."
-- "Stocks look a little tired here. We could get a little more of an up move but then trade flat with a downward bias."

Like many other analysts, Pizzo does not expect any change in monetary policy later today. "There are two camps. The major one thinks inflation is benign and the minor one thinks the consumer will pick up spending next year, which will again pressure rates."
